findings.issue: contradicts task clause (5) 'a finding citing no line of the phase diff is a note, not a block': sort_findings sends such a finding to the validation pass like any other (a candidate), and when the pass confirms it as correctness/requirement it lands in 'unowned', which review_findings_step turns into a stop for a human (a block, not a note). tests/test_drive_phase.py pv8 (~2426-2441) and pv1 (pv-outside is in the validation prompt, ~197) pin this behaviour, so the suite now asserts the opposite of the clause. This is the orchestrator's 'positive evidence only' rule; it is a deliberate departure from the task text and the task description was not amended.
findings.resolution: Either amend the task's clause (5) and acceptance text to the 'positive evidence' rule (a finding citing no phase-diff line is validated like the rest and only a human-settled stop if confirmed), or restore the clause: make a finding whose cited_ranges overlap no task's diff a note without a block. Decide which and record it, so the task description, pv1/pv8 and phase-signoff.md agree.

findings.issue: contradicts task clause (1) 'a finding the second pass withdraws does not block and is recorded as a note': a withdrawal (or confirmed-as-other) of a med-or-worse finding is not taken unless the stream holds a Read/NotebookRead/Grep tool_use naming a file the finding cites; otherwise validation_step stops the whole drive. A finding whose `file` names no path (cited_paths empty) can therefore never be withdrawn by any pass, and always stops.
findings.resolution: If the read-evidence rule is kept, amend clause (1) to say so and make the unreadable case explicit (a finding citing no path cannot be demoted: stop with that reason, not 'read nothing'); otherwise record the unread withdrawal as the note it asked for.

findings.issue: The read evidence only counts Read, NotebookRead and Grep with a file `path`. VALIDATE_HEAD/VALIDATE_RULE tell the pass to 're-read' and to use 'git show <commit>' but never name the Read tool, so a pass that opens the code with Bash (git show, sed -n, cat) or Grep over a directory is treated as having read nothing and its withdrawal stops the drive (a false stop on honest work).
findings.resolution: Say in VALIDATE_RULE that each cited file is opened with the Read tool, or count the Bash opening commands (git show/cat/sed) in stream_reads.
